source_line: Source: Associated Press market close, Nov. 23, 2026
caption:
Wall Street just had one of its biggest days ever — and if you own a 401(k), you own this bounce.

On Monday the S&P 500 jumped 326.78 points (about 4.7%) to 7,237.17 — its second-biggest one-day POINT gain on record, behind only April 9, 2025 (Associated Press, Nov. 23). The Nasdaq soared 6.5% and the Dow rose 3%. It snapped a seven-day losing streak that had pulled the S&P more than 10% below its record.

The spark: Nvidia surged about 31% — roughly $950 billion in market value — after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

Why it matters even if you never watch the market: the S&P 500 is the backbone of most retirement accounts, so a 4.7% up day lifted the balance millions are saving. Monday clawed back over half of last week's drop.

My take: one monster day is a relief, not an all-clear — the 'fear gauge' (the VIX) still sits near 27, and it was a record in points, not in percent. A 401(k) is measured in decades, not Mondays.
